'''''Potamogeton gramineus''''' is a species of [[aquatic plant]] known by the common name '''various-leaved pondweed''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''variableleaf pondweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=POGR8|taxon=Potamogeton gramineus|accessdate=13 October 2015}}</ref>  '''grass-leaved pondweed''' or '''grassy pondweed''', native to the northern hemisphere where it grows in shallow, clean water.

==Description==
This is an aquatic [[perennial]] growing from a creeping [[rhizome]] that anchors in wet [[Substrate (biology)|substrate]]. It produces thin, cylindrical, heavily branching stems usually less than a metre in length. The submerged leaves are [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]], relatively narrow, typically 40–90 mm long and 5–12 mm wide along the main stem but smaller on the side branches.<ref name='Preston'/> They are translucent and pale green with a white [[midrib]], and finely toothed. Floating leaves are more oval in shape, 20–70 mm long by 7–34 mm wide,<ref name='Preston'/> and borne on long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. The [[inflorescence]] is a short spike of many flowers arising from the water on a stout [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]].

This species readily [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridizes]] with many other species of ''[[Potamogeton]]''. Hybrids have been recorded with ''[[Potamogeton perfoliatus|P. perfoliatus]]'' (''P''. × ''nitens'' <small>Weber</small>), ''[[Potamogeton lucens|P. lucens]]'' (''P.'' × ''angustifolius'' <small>J.Presl.</small>), ''[[Potamogeton natans|P. natans]]'' (''P''. × ''sparganiifolius'' <small>Laest. ex Fr.</small>), ''[[Potamogeton coloratus|P. coloratus]]'' (''P''. × ''billupsii'' <small>Fryer</small>), ''[[Potamogeton maackianus|P. maackianus]]'' (''P.'' × ''biwaensis'' <small>Miki</small>), ''[[Potamogeton illinoensis|P. illinoensis]]'' (''P.'' × ''spathuliformis'' <small>(J.W.Robbins) Morong</small>), ''[[Potamogeton richardsonii|P. richardsonii]]'' (''P.'' × ''hagstromii'' <small>A.Benn.</small>), [[Potamogeton alpinus|''P. alpinus'']] (''P.'' × ''nericius'' <small>Hagstr.</small>), ''[[Potamogeton nodosus|P. nodosus]]'' (''P.'' × ''lanceolatifolius'' <small>(Tiselius) C.D.Preston</small>), ''P. oakesianus'' (''P.'' × ''mirabilis'' <small>Z.Kaplan, Hellq. & Fehrer</small>) and ''[[Potamogeton polygonifolius|P. polygonifolius]]''.<ref name='Preston'/><ref name=kwc2/> In Britain, ''P''. x ''nitens'' and ''P''. x ''angustifolius'' are quite common. Recent molecular analysis has shown that Swedish collections of the putative hybrid ''P. gramineus'' x ''P. polygonifolius'' are in fact ''P. gramineus'' x ''P. nodosus''.<ref name=Kaplan/>

A triple hybrid, ''P. gramineus'' × ''lucens'' × ''perfoliatus'' (''P''. × ''torssandrii'' <small>(Tiselius) Dörfler</small>), is also known.

As well as hybridising frequently, various-leaved pondweed is an extremely variable plant and care should be taken with its identification.<ref name='Preston'/>

==Taxonomy==
''Potamogeton gramineus'' (gramineus meaning 'grasslike') was one of the original species named by [[Carl Linnaeus|Linnaeus]] in ''[[Species Plantarum]]'' (1753). However, due to its highly variable nature and propensity for hybridisation, various-leaved pondweed has received a bewildering number of synonyms.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}

DNA analysis indicates that ''P. gramineus'' is one of the broad-leaved pondweed clade (section ''Potamogeton'') and is probably most closely related to the [[Potamogeton lucens|''P. lucens'']] group.<ref name=Lind/>

==Distribution==
''Potamogeton gramineus'' is native to much of the Northern Hemisphere, with a [[Holarctic realm|Holarctic]] distribution. It occurs in northern Europe (Britain,<ref name='Preston'/> Ireland, Iceland, Scandinavia, Germany, Switzerland, France, Poland, Russia, the Baltic States),<ref name=Sweden/><ref name='Guo'/> Greenland, North America (US except for the southeast, Canada).<ref name=Sweden/><ref name=USDA/> There are outlying populations in southern Europe (Iberia, Corsica, Italy), [[Caucasus]], [[Pyrenees]], and western US.<ref name=Sweden/>
[[File:Potamogeton gramineus cultivated.JPG|thumb|Various-leaved pondweed, ''Potamogeton gramineus'', in a garden pond.]]

==Ecology and conservation==
Various-leaved pondweed grows in various water body types including ponds, lakes, bogs, ditches and streams. It is usually restricted to shallower water <1 m deep,<ref name='Preston'/> though it has been recorded growing at more than 5 m depth in very clear, oligotrophic water in Llynnau Cregennen, Wales.<ref name=Gold/> It is intolerant of [[nutrient pollution]] and is not usually found in base-poor water of alkalinity less than about 200 μEq/L. The roots penetrate to a depth of about 10 cm.<ref name=Fort/> In Michigan streams, ''P. gramineus'' is restricted to riffles with warmer interstitial temperatures.<ref name=Fort/>

Grazing by waterfowl can have a significant effect on various-leaved pondweed. In Sentiz Lake (Leon, Spain), ''P. gramineus'' was sparse and the dominant plants were ''[[Ceratophyllum demersum]]'' and ''[[Myriophyllum spicatum]]''. However, within experimental cages from which waterfowl were excluded, ''P. gramineus'' became co-dominant and developed both flowers and floating leaves.<ref name=Rodrig/>

In Britain, it has shown the same pattern of decline as other broad-leaved pondweeds such as ''[[Potamogeton praelongus|P. praelongus]]'' and ''[[Potamogeton alpinus|P. alpinus]]'', with most losses occurring in southern Britain,<ref name=NewAt/> and is now classed as near threatened in England.<ref name='Stroh'/> This likely reflects increasing eutrophication, canalization of rivers leading to loss of backwater habitats and other floodplain standing waters, and degradation or loss of pond and lake habitats. ''P. gramineus'' may also grow in open reedbeds, and the loss of traditional reed cutting practices may have caused the loss of populations from this habitat. It is Critically Endangered in the Czech Republic,<ref name=Grulich/> Endangered in Germany,<ref name=floraw/> Flanders<ref name=vanL/> and Switzerland,<ref name=Moser/> Near Threatened in the Netherlands,<ref name=Sparrius/> and scarce and of conservation importance in Spain.<ref name=Fern/> Local extinction has also been recorded in Lower Saxony between 1948 and 1986.<ref name=WiegBrux/> In the US, ''P. gramineus'' is listed as Threatened in Illinois and Endangered in Ohio and Pennsylvania.<ref name='USDA'/>

Indices of environmental tolerance using trophic ranking schemes in Europe tend to show ''P. gramineus'' to be one of the more nutrient-sensitive aquatic plants.<ref name=lakeleaf/><ref name=rivleaf/><ref name=macfree/> Studies in the Netherlands show ''P. gramineus'' to be associated with ''Littorelletea'' lakes, and to be one of a suite of species sensitive to [[Acid rain|acidification]].<ref name=Roelofs/>
Various-leaved pondweed is one of the so-called ''Magnopotamion'' group of pondweeds. These are a characteristic floristic component of the protected [[Habitats Directive]] habitat Type 'Natural eutrophic lakes with Magnopotamion'.<ref name=JNCC/> However, in Britain ''P. gramineus'' also occurs in waters with lower nutrient concentrations and is considered a characteristic species of mesotrophic lakes.<ref name=doeni/>

==Cultivation==
''Potamogeton gramineus'' is not in general cultivation, though it is an attractive plant and grows well in a garden pond<ref name=Pondolive/> or barrel. Its slower growth than most submerged species, attractive leaves and habit of producing a limited number of floating leaves make it very ornamental and suitable for garden ponds, and its smaller size than many other pondweeds is also a benefit. In common with other pondweeds of this group it roots poorly from stem cuttings and is best propagated by division of the rhizomes.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}
